stories.text: Saying he's tired of seeing his Baltimore Orioles "lose and lose and lose", club owner Edward Bennett Williams fires Hank Peters, the club's general manager (GM) since November 1975. Peters, 63, twice won The Sporting News Executive of the Year Award during his 12 years in office—with two pennants and a World Series (1983)—but Baltimore has gone 140–184 (.432) over the past two seasons.
stories.headline: Orioles Fire GM Hank Peters, 63, After Two Losing Seasons

stories.text: The New York Giants clinch the National League pennant on the last day of the season with a 5–3 win coupled with the Boston Beaneaters 6–1 loss. It was the first time in major league history that the pennant was determined on the last day of the season.

stories.text: Pud Galvin of the Pittsburgh Alleghenys becomes the first pitcher to record 300 career wins with a 5–1 victory over the Washington Nationals.
stories.headline: Galvin Wins 300th Career Game, Pittsburgh Beats Nationals 5-1

image.alt: Standing man in baseball uniform cap, vest, knickers; caption reads J. Galvin, P. Pittsburgh.

stories.extract: James Francis "Pud" Galvin was an American professional baseball pitcher in the 19th century. He was the first 300-game winner in the major leagues and was posthumously inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1965.

stories.text: Charlie Sweeney and Henry Boyle of the St. Louis Maroons combine on a 5 inning no-hitter when the game is called on account of rain. Despite the no-hitter, the Maroons lose 1–0 when 2 errors allow the only run of the game.
stories.headline: Sweeney and Boyle Combine on No-Hitter, Maroons Lose 1-0
stories.extract: Charles Joseph Sweeney was an American Major League Baseball pitcher from 1883 through 1887. He played for the Providence Grays, St. Louis Maroons, and Cleveland Blues, and is best known for his performance in 1884, when he won 41 games.
